content_voiceover: This is the five-year update of the POLARIX trial, comparing Pola-R-CHP against standard R-CHOP in the global intention-to-treat population, four hundred forty patients versus four hundred thirty-nine. Look at how the two progression-free survival curves separate early and then stay apart. At the primary analysis, two years, event-free rate was seventy-six point seven percent with Pola-R-CHP versus seventy point two percent with R-CHOP, a hazard ratio of zero point seven three. At the three-year update, seventy-one point eight versus sixty-four point one percent, hazard ratio zero point seven six. And now at the five-year update, sixty-four point nine percent versus fifty-nine point one percent, hazard ratio zero point seven seven. Notice the hazard ratio barely moves across three separate readouts, which tells you this isn't an early effect that washes out, it's a durable, sustained separation. This is the trial that justified moving polatuzumab vedotin into the first-line, category one option for higher-risk DLBCL, specifically smIPI greater than one or IPI two or higher, as you saw on the previous regimens slide.

keypoint_voiceover: The key number to remember is the hazard ratio, roughly zero point seven three to zero point seven seven, and it stays essentially flat from the two-year primary analysis all the way to the five-year update. That durability is what earned Pola-R-CHP its category one first-line status for smIPI greater than one or IPI two or higher DLBCL. Five-year PFS lands at about sixty-five percent with Pola-R-CHP versus fifty-nine percent with R-CHOP.
